angle: How NASA accounted for its Bennu sample

items.claim: OSIRIS-REx returned Bennu material to Earth on September 24, 2023.
items.synthesisExcerpt: OSIRIS-REx returned material from asteroid Bennu to Earth on September 24, 2023.
items.sourceEvidence: Provided operator paraphrase of the NASA source: OSIRIS-REx returned material from Bennu to Earth on September 24, 2023.
items.qualification: The synthesis does not specify the amount returned on that date.

items.claim: The mission required at least 60 grams of asteroid material.
items.synthesisExcerpt: The mission required at least 60 grams of asteroid material.
items.sourceEvidence: Provided operator paraphrase of the NASA source: the mission required at least 60 grams.
items.usefulness: Sets the benchmark for accounting for the sample.
items.qualification: This is the mission requirement, not the final inventory.

items.claim: The team exceeded the 60-gram requirement before completely opening the sampling head.
items.synthesisExcerpt: The team exceeded that requirement before completely opening the sampling head.
items.sourceEvidence: Provided operator paraphrase of the NASA source: the team exceeded the requirement before completely opening the sampling head.
items.usefulness: Shows the requirement was met before the sampling head was fully opened.
items.qualification: The synthesis gives no amount for this earlier milestone.

items.sourceEvidence: Provided operator paraphrase of the NASA source: a final pour added 51.2 grams.
items.usefulness: Identifies a specific addition during final accounting.
items.qualification: The synthesis does not state the amount present before this pour.

items.claim: The completed inventory amounted to 121.6 grams.
items.synthesisExcerpt: The completed inventory amounted to 121.6 grams.
items.sourceEvidence: Provided operator paraphrase of the NASA source: the completed inventory amounted to 121.6 grams.
items.qualification: The synthesis does not break down the full inventory by component.
